findings.title: Referer-based embed authorization is weak and sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL
findings.body: `ensure_embeddable` trusts the client-supplied Referer host and then sets `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL`. A Referer can be forged or stripped by non-browser clients. When the check passes, the page can be framed by any site. Rendering also runs for logged-in users with their cookies, so clickjacking is possible. Prefer a `frame-ancestors` CSP restricted to `embeddable_host`. The check also ignores scheme and port. Subdomains of the host are not handled, so legitimate embeds there fail.

findings.title: embed_url is not validated against embeddable_host before enqueueing, and the job is enqueued on every miss
findings.body: `embed_url` comes straight from the query string. A Referer check is the only guard, and `TopicRetriever` checks the host only later in the job. Every miss enqueues a Sidekiq job, so an attacker can flood the queue with arbitrary URLs. The `loading` page also auto-reloads every 30s, which enqueues another job each time. Validate the URL's host synchronously in the controller before enqueueing.

findings.title: Unescaped request.referer interpolated into inline JavaScript
findings.body: `'<%= request.referer %>'` is HTML-escaped by ERB but is placed inside a JS string in a `<script>` block. The Referer header is only checked on its host component. A path or query string containing a quote or backslash, or a newline, can break out of the string or cause JS errors. HTML escaping does not make the value safe in a JS context. Also, the full Referer URL is used as the `postMessage` targetOrigin, which must be an origin only. Use the origin (`scheme://host[:port]`) via `to_json`/`j`.

findings.title: Weak postMessage origin check via indexOf
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring test. An empty or short origin string, or an origin that is a substring of `discourseUrl`, passes. For example, origin `http://a` matches `http://a.example.com/`. Compare `e.origin` for exact equality with the origin of `discourseUrl`.

findings.title: contents mutated with << and footer is added before the sha1 is computed on each import
findings.body: `contents << ...` mutates the caller's string in place. This can raise FrozenError for frozen strings and has side effects on the caller. The link is also interpolated unescaped into an HTML attribute (`'<a href='#{url}'>`). Separately, `import_remote` and the feed importer pass content straight from remote sources, which then go into a raw_html post with no sanitization (see `Post#cook`). That makes stored XSS possible.

findings.title: raw_html cook method skips all sanitization
findings.body: When `cook_method` is `raw_html`, `cook` returns `raw` untouched. Content fetched from remote sites or RSS feeds is stored and later rendered with `raw post.cooked` in the embed view and in the main site. Scripts and event handlers in the feed content run in the forum's origin. ruby-readability sanitizes only to a limited degree, and the RSS path (`CGI.unescapeHTML` of feed content) has no sanitizer at all. The content should be sanitized, for example with Sanitize.

findings.title: Kernel#open on admin-configured URL (and in import_remote)
findings.body: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses open-uri's `Kernel#open`. A value beginning with `|` runs a shell command, and a path reads local files. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does the same with `open(url).read`. There the URL is supplied by the embedding page and only its host is checked. Use `URI.parse(...).open` or RestClient with an http(s) scheme check. This is also a possible SSRF vector.

findings.title: Feed item handling not nil-safe and one bad item aborts the whole run
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when an item has no `content`. Many RSS feeds only supply `description`, and `String#scrub` also requires Ruby 2.1+. Any exception in `TopicEmbed.import` aborts the loop for all remaining items. The job has `retry: false`. `feed_key` is defined but never used, so there is no conditional-GET caching and the whole feed is re-fetched hourly.

findings.title: Non-atomic setnx + expire throttle
findings.body: If the process dies between `setnx` and `expire`, the key never expires. That URL is then blocked forever for non-staff users. Use `SET key value EX 60 NX`, or `setex`-style semantics.

findings.title: Spec expects TopicRetriever.new in the request, but the controller enqueues a job
findings.body: The controller calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`. The spec expects `TopicRetriever.new` and `retrieve` to be invoked during the request. This only works if jobs execute inline in test. Even then it is an indirect assertion. The test does not verify that the job is enqueued with the right arguments.

findings.title: Revising a raw_html post may re-cook and drop content
findings.body: `Post#before_save` re-cooks via `cook(raw, topic_id: ...)`. For raw_html posts this returns raw, which is fine. `TopicEmbed.import` also calls `absolutize_urls` on update, but computes `content_sha1` from the pre-absolutize contents. The `bypass_rate_limiter` option is respected, but `revise!` returns false when the absolutized raw equals the stored raw. In that case `embed.update_column(:content_sha1)` is still executed, which is fine. A missing post (`embed.post` nil) would raise on `PostRevisor.new(nil)`.

findings.title: Unrelated edit to an existing migration adds force: true
findings.body: `force: true` on `create_table` drops the table if it exists. The edit is made to an already-existing migration, which is unrelated to this PR. It is risky if the migration is ever re-run. The unrelated whitespace changes in `20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` are noise as well.

findings.title: create_table with force: true drops existing table
findings.body: `force: true` will silently drop any existing `topic_embeds` table and its data when the migration is run. It is also not reversible in an obvious way. The `topic_id` and `post_id` columns have no indexes, although `where(topic_id:)` is used.

findings.title: Invalid ERB `<%- end if %>` and posts-present check mislabelled
findings.body: `<%- end if %>` is a syntax error in ERB/Ruby. `end if` requires a condition and is not a valid terminator for the `if/else` block. The template will fail to compile, so the embed page would never render. In addition, the branch logic is inverted from a readable standpoint: 'Discussion Highlights' is shown only when posts exist. A topic with only the first post would show 'Begin the Discussion'.

findings.title: Header text depends on posts but view assumes topic_view is set after TopicView.new with nil topic
findings.body: `TopicView.new` could raise for a deleted or inaccessible topic. `topic_id_for_embed` returns an id even if the topic was trashed, which results in an error page inside the iframe. There is no handling.
